summary.headline: MARA (-6.47%) and HOOD (-5.76%) both extend a second straight session of outsized declines against Friday's broad selloff (SPY -1.0%, QQQ -1.5% on a chip-sector rout tied to a new Chinese AI model plus US-Iran tensions) — MARA persisting RED on its Bitcoin-derivative thesis risk, HOOD persisting RED after closing below $100 on Bloomberg-reported credit-card ABS scrutiny. flags.headline: MARA -6.47%: second straight session of Bitcoin-driven weakness compresses the thesis's existential risk case
flags.detail: MARA fell -6.47% ($11.44→$10.70), extending Friday's -6.84% drop. No new company-specific catalyst identified; Bitcoin continues to drift lower (~$63.4K, down from ~$65.0K on 07-15) on a persistent spot-ETF outflow streak. A family trust's routine 16,000-share sale (~$174K, disclosed under Rule 144) is immaterial and not a driver.
flags.thesis_link: Matches MARA key_risk #1/#3: GAAP losses and revenue are 'essentially a leveraged derivative of Bitcoin price' with existential risk if crypto enters a prolonged downturn. Second consecutive session of this risk materializing.

evidence.source: TradersUnion — Marathon Digital drops on bitcoin mining competition
Yahoo Finance — Bitcoin USD price history

flags.headline: HOOD -5.76%: closes below $100 for the first time this cycle as credit-expansion scrutiny and broad selloff compound
flags.detail: Robinhood fell -5.76% ($106.06→$99.91), closing below the $100 level after Friday's -8.15% drop. Bloomberg reported (via Benzinga/Investing.com) that Robinhood is marketing at least $400M (potentially up to $500M) of credit-card-backed asset-backed securities in four parts — investors are scrutinizing the credit-risk implications of the consumer-lending push. ARK Invest continued trimming its position (~$3.2M sold) on top of a broader Nasdaq pullback (-1.1% to -1.5%). Two-session cumulative decline is now roughly -13%.
flags.thesis_link: Matches HOOD key_risk #1: 'Forward P/E of 41.5x... leave minimal margin of safety' — the stock's amplified reaction to the ABS/credit story reflects that thin cushion. The credit-expansion angle itself is not yet an enumerated key_risk; worth adding to the thesis on the next full screener refresh.

evidence.source: Benzinga — Why Is Robinhood Stock Falling on Friday? (citing Bloomberg ABS report)
FXLeaders — Robinhood slides toward $100 on credit expansion, fundraising scrutiny

flags.headline: SYK -3.44%: reverses Thursday's dividend-raise bounce as Q2 cyber-recovery concerns resurface ahead of July 30 earnings
flags.detail: Stryker fell -3.44% ($331.12→$319.74), giving back Thursday's +4.68% bounce. Reporting attributes the move to investor caution ahead of the July 30 Q2 print and lingering doubt about the full financial recovery from the March 11 cyberattack (Iran-linked 'Handala' group; Microsoft Intune device-wipe). Stryker's own filings show the March incident already dented Q1 revenue/EPS despite systems being restored by early April.
flags.thesis_link: Matches SYK key_risk #2: 'March 2026 cybersecurity incident... raising concerns about IT infrastructure resilience and potential recurring cyber exposure.' Direct match — thesis risk resurfacing ahead of the quarter that will show whether the disruption is fully behind the company.

evidence.source: QuiverQuant — Stryker Slides As Investors Reassess Cyberattack Recovery Ahead Of Q2 Results
The Record (Recorded Future News) — Stryker says malware was involved in recent cyberattack

flags.note: Sourcing is trade-press (QuiverQuant, Recorded Future), not tier-1 financial press — unconfirmed by Reuters/Bloomberg/WSJ for today's specific reaction. Capped at AMBER on evidence quality per guardrail, despite the clean thesis match.

flags.headline: TOL -3.19%: swept into rate-sensitive housing weakness despite a recent Citi upgrade and raised guidance
flags.detail: Toll Brothers fell -3.19% ($155.66→$150.70). No TOL-specific negative news found — Citi upgraded to Buy (PT $176) on 07-05 and another analyst raised its target to $176 on 07-10, and the company raised FY2026 delivery guidance. The move looks more macro-driven: Friday's broad selloff plus rising gas prices from US-Iran tensions feeding into rate-sensitivity for luxury housing. Independently, GuruFocus flags the stock as ~15% above its GF Value estimate with $13.5M in insider selling (no buying) over the past three months — a valuation/alignment watch item, not a new catalyst.
flags.thesis_link: Soft match to TOL key_risk #2: 'sustained elevated mortgage rates or a stock market correction could simultaneously reduce demand and compress pricing.' Today's broad market correction is exactly that scenario, though not yet a rate move specifically.

evidence.source: GuruFocus — Toll Brothers Inc (TOL) Shares Fall 4.5%

flags.headline: CRDO -2.90%: AI-capex rout stabilizing but not resolved — downgraded from RED
flags.detail: Credo fell a further -2.90% ($208.26→$202.23), a much smaller move than Friday's -8.12%, suggesting Friday's TSMC-capex-driven chip selloff is stabilizing rather than deepening. Downgrading RED→AMBER on reduced daily magnitude; not yet resolved to green given the valuation cushion is still thin and the hyperscaler capex earnings window (GOOG 07-22) is the next real test.
flags.thesis_link: Matches CRDO key_risk #1 (extreme valuation, no margin for error on AI capex slowdown). Persisting since 2026-06-28, severity reduced today.

evidence.source: 247WallSt — Marvell drops 8% as AI capex slowdown fears weigh on chips

flags.headline: FAST -2.57%: continuing to digest the July 14 gross-margin miss
flags.detail: Fastenal fell -2.57% ($46.66→$45.46), extending the -3.67% drop on its July 14 earnings day. Q2 2026 revenue grew 14.7% YoY and EPS of $0.33 matched estimates (drop shows a small -1.29% surprise vs. consensus), but gross margin declined 75bp YoY, which is what the market is punishing despite the strong topline.
flags.thesis_link: Matches FAST key_risk #3: 'tariff risk on imported industrial products could compress margins.' The realized 75bp gross-margin decline is that risk materializing.

evidence.source: GuruFocus — Fastenal (FAST) Reports Strong Q2 2026 Earnings with 14.7% Sales Growth
